source_text: CAPUT DUODECIMUM, De immensitate Dei. Haec de quarto Dei attributo, nempe immutabilitate: sequitur quintum. Immensitas, quae est summa DEI perfectio, qua ille expers est circumscriptionis et praesentiae localis definitae ad certum determinatumque spatium. Materiale quidem etiam in hoc attributo idem est quod in aliis, eminentissima videlicet DEI perfectio. Formale vero in negatione circumscriptionis et praesentiae localis definitae. Ex quo sequitur, positis jam creaturis et locis, omnipraesentia sive ubiquitas, quae triplici ratione considerari potest: 1. ratione cognitionis; 2. ratione voluntariae operationis; 3. ratione essentiae, quam tertiam potissimum afferimus quando Deum dicimus immensum et hinc omnipraesentem.
english: CHAPTER TWELVE. On the immensity of God.

These things concerning the fourth attribute of God, namely immutability: there follows the fifth. Immensity, which is GOD's highest perfection, by which He is free from circumscription and from local presence defined to a certain and determined space.

The material in this attribute also is the same as in the others, namely GOD's most eminent perfection. But the formal consists in the negation of circumscription and of defined local presence. From which, creatures and places now being posited, there follows omnipresence or ubiquity, which can be considered in a threefold ratio: of knowledge; of voluntary operation; of essence — which third we chiefly allege when we call God immense and hence omnipresent.

source_text: Esse autem ubique dicitur Deus ad modulum captus nostri, cum potius res sint in DEO, ex quo, per quem et in quo omnia, Rom. XI.36. Act. XVII.25,27,28. Parmenides arguit: Si unum est, non est in se, neque in alio. Sed illud nos non ferit, quia Deum dicimus esse in se secundum nostrum intelligendi modum, et exponimus negative, Deum esse in se, id est, non in alio. Jeremias tamen etiam XXIII.24. Deo tribuit, quod caelum ac terram impleat. Utrumque vero Scriptura docet, quia uterque sensus est verus: ille dignior Deo, hic vero intelligentiae nostrae convenientior.
english: But God is said to be everywhere to the measure of our grasp, when rather things are in GOD, from whom, through whom, and in whom are all things in Romans 11:36 and Acts 17:25, 27-28.

Parmenides argues: If the One is, it is not in itself, nor in another. But that does not strike us, because we say God is in Himself according to our mode of understanding, and we explain it negatively: God is in Himself, that is, not in another. Yet Jeremiah 23:24 also attributes to God that He fills heaven and earth. Scripture teaches both, because each sense is true: that one worthier of God, this one more fitted to our intelligence.

source_text: Tria demonstrabimus. I. Deum omnia loca et spatia hujus mundi immensitate essentiae suae implere, sive ubique praesentem esse. PRIMA ratio: Qui simul est in caelis, in sepulchro, in extremitate maris, in imis partibus terrae, is immensitate essentiae suae omnia loca et spatia hujus mundi implet. Atqui Deus simul est his omnibus in locis, Psal. CXXXIX; Sap. I.7; Isa. LXVI.1; Jer. XXIII.24; I Reg. VIII.27; Act. VII.49; XVII.27; Eph. IV.6. SECUNDA ab infinita perfectione Dei. TERTIA ab incommodo seu absurdo: si Deus secundum substantiam non est alibi quam in caelo, sequitur Christum in terris versantem non fuisse verum Deum. QUARTA ab immediata Dei operatione. QUINTA a catholico consensu piae antiquitatis — Cyprianus, Ambrosius, Hieronymus, Augustinus, Athanasius, Tertullianus, Justinus.
english: We will demonstrate three things. I. That God fills all places and spaces of this world by the immensity of His essence, or is present everywhere. FIRST reason: Whoever is at once in the heavens, in the grave, at the extremity of the sea, in the lowest parts of the earth, fills all places and spaces of this world by the immensity of His essence. But God is at once in all these places, as Psalm 139, Wisdom 1:7, Isaiah 66:1, Jeremiah 23:24, 1 Kings 8:27, Acts 7:49 and 17:27, and Ephesians 4:6 testify.

SECOND, from God's infinite perfection. THIRD, from inconvenience or absurdity: if God according to substance is nowhere but in heaven, it follows that Christ sojourning on earth was not true God. FOURTH, from God's immediate operation. FIFTH, from the catholic consent of pious antiquity — Cyprian, Ambrose, Jerome, Augustine, Athanasius, Tertullian, Justin.

source_text: II. Deus secundum substantiam suam non definitur aut circumscribitur hujus mundi spatiis, sed etiam extra hunc mundum est. PRIMA ratio a testimonio sacrae Scripturae: I Reg. VIII.27. Caeli caelorum te non capiant. Job XI.8. Excelsior caelo est et profundior inferno. SECUNDA ab infinitate. TERTIA a catholico consensu — Chrysostomus, Augustinus; Hermes Trismegistus: Deum esse circulum, cujus centrum ubique est, circumferentia nusquam. Extra hunc orbem Deus est in seipso, sicut ante hunc orbem conditum. Extra mundum est uno duntaxat modo, per substantiam. III. Nulla creatura potest esse ubique praesens per immensitatem essentiae, quia absoluta Dei perfectio nulli creaturae formaliter communicari potest.
english: II. God according to His substance is not defined or circumscribed by this world's spaces, but is also outside this world. FIRST reason from the testimony of sacred Scripture: 1 Kings 8:27, The heaven of heavens cannot contain You. Job 11:8, Higher than heaven and deeper than hell. SECOND from infinity. THIRD from catholic consent — Chrysostom, Augustine; Hermes Trismegistus: God is a circle whose center is everywhere, circumference nowhere.

Outside this orb God is in Himself, as before this orb was founded. Outside the world He is in only one mode, by substance. III. No creature can be present everywhere by immensity of essence, because God's absolute perfection cannot be formally communicated to any creature.

source_text: ERRAT igitur CONR. VORSTIUS a Scoto, Bodino, Taurello deceptus, Notis ad disp. III. p.232 de Deo, quia contra catholicum consensum et doctissimum Zanchium docet, Deum secundum substantiam suam non esse alibi quam in caelo. Allegrat rationes septem. VERUM error iste a duplici confusione est: non distinguit sermonis divini potentiam propriam ab impropria de throno et habitatione; et a specialis praesentiae aspectu ipsam immensitatem essentiae evertit. Deus enim speciali ratione in humanitate Christi per unionem hypostaticam, in sanctis per cognitionem et amorem, in Ecclesia per auxilium, in caelo per majestatem et gloriam — manente tamen essentiae immensitate ubique.
english: Therefore Conrad Vorstius errs, deceived by Scotus, Bodin, and Taurellus, in Notes on Disputation III On God p. 232, because against the catholic consensus and the most learned Zanchi he teaches that God according to His substance is nowhere but in heaven. He alleges seven reasons.

But that error is from a double confusion: it does not distinguish Scripture's proper from improper speech about throne and dwelling; and from the aspect of special presence it overturns the very immensity of essence. For God is in a special ratio in Christ's humanity by hypostatic union, in the saints by knowledge and love, in the Church by help, in heaven by majesty and glory — the immensity of essence nonetheless remaining everywhere.

source_text: REGULAE. 1. Immensitas Dei spectatur absolute aut relate — absolute ab aeterno; relate partim omnipraesentia, partim incomprehensibilitas. 2. Modus immensitatis divinae concipiendus est absque ulla multiplicatione, extensione, aut partium divisione. 3. Deus est in omni loco, non ut locatum, sed ut causa et dominus cujusque loci. 4. Deus est ubique non per extensionem essentiae suae, sed per comprehensionem. 5. Deus est extra mundum non mole, sed infinitate essentiae. 6. Deus ita est in caelis et sanctis majestate, gratia et gloria sua, ut tamen sit ubique essentia et potentia sua. 7. Cum Deus in sanctis inest per gratiam, praesentia quandoque latet, quandoque patet. 8. Praesentia Dei est generalis, specialis et specialissima. 9. Ubique esse Deo non est indecorum. 10. Loca Scripturae quae Deo tribuunt magnitudinem, thronum, domum, intelligenda sunt quatenus immensitati essentiae ipsius convenienter. 11. Immensitatem Dei imitari debemus immenso desiderio aeternitatis.
english: RULES. 1. God's immensity is regarded absolutely or relatively — absolutely from eternity; relatively partly as omnipresence, partly as incomprehensibility. 2. The mode of divine immensity is to be conceived without any multiplication, extension, or division of parts. 3. God is in every place not as located, but as cause and lord of each place. 4. God is everywhere not by extension of His essence, but by comprehension. 5. God is outside the world not by bulk, but by infinity of essence.

6. God is so in the heavens and saints by His majesty, grace, and glory that He is nonetheless everywhere by essence and power. 7. When God is in the saints by grace, presence sometimes is hidden, sometimes open. 8. God's presence is general, special, and most special. 9. To be everywhere is not unseemly for God. 10. Scripture places that attribute greatness, throne, house to God are to be understood as far as they suit the immensity of His essence. 11. We ought to imitate God's immensity by immense desire of eternity.
